sections.title: Quick Answer
sections.content: The best **prayer journal app for iPhone** in 2026 is a real journaling app — Amen. or Echo Prayer are the strongest picks — paired with FaithWall (free to download) as the layer that gets you back into it. A journal you never reopen isn't a journal, it's a graveyard for requests. FaithWall puts today's prayer on your lock screen so you see it without deciding to open anything.

sections.text: Search "**prayer journal app iphone 2026**" and you'll get the same handful of names in every roundup: Amen., Echo Prayer, PrayerMate, Prayer Notebook. They're all real, and none of them is lying about what it does — track requests, mark answers, keep a running record you can look back on. FaithWall isn't one of them. It doesn't hold entries or dates. What it does is put today's prayer in front of you on the one screen you check without deciding to, so the journal you picked doesn't quietly go read-only.

This isn't a listicle padded to hit a word count. The four apps below are verified live on the App Store this month, with real prices and real feature sets — because the honest answer to which **prayer journal app** wins depends on whether you want cards, feeds, or AI prompts.
The honest shortlist: four real prayer journal apps

Each of these does something the others don't, and none of them is a job FaithWall competes for — FaithWall doesn't attempt journaling. Pick the one that matches how you actually think about your prayer list.

items: **Amen. Christian Prayer Journal** — free base app, with an Amen+ subscription at $2.99/month or $14.99/year and a 7-day trial. AI-suggested prompts and voice-recorded entries help if a blank page stalls you before you start.

**Echo Prayer** (The Parable Group) — free, with an optional $15/year ECHO+ tier. Built around marking requests answered over time, which makes it the closest thing to a literal digital prayer journal on this list.

**PrayerMate** (Geero.net) — free, with an optional Patron subscription around $2.99/month to support development. Card-based, with feeds like Operation World's country-of-the-day built in for intercession beyond your own list.
**Prayer Notebook** (Kalon Creative) — free, over 70,000 downloads, no subscription tier at all. Schedule prayers by day, attach a photo, mark answered. The simplest option here by a wide margin.

sections.text: So which one should you actually download?

If you want the closest thing to a real journal — dated entries, an answered-prayer archive you can scroll back through — **Echo Prayer** is the strongest pick, and it's the same app our [best prayer app for iPhone](/blog/best-prayer-app-for-iphone) roundup ranks for intercession. If you want zero subscription and don't need feeds, Prayer Notebook is the honest free option. If blank-page paralysis is the actual problem, Amen.'s AI prompts solve a real thing. None of that changes what happens next: whichever one you pick has to survive being closed.

A **prayer journal app** only works if you reopen it. FaithWall doesn't hold your entries — it holds today's request or verse on your lock screen, so the app you just picked has a reason to be opened again tomorrow instead of just once.

items: Download **FaithWall** from the App Store — free to download.
Open it and pick the verses you want to pray through.
Tap **Set Lock Screen** — FaithWall applies it through an Apple Shortcut in about 60 seconds.
Every time you unlock your phone, that request is the first thing you see — not a notification, your actual prayer.
Once it's answered, that's your cue to open your journal app and write it down properly.

sections.content: **FaithWall isn't a journal — it's the reminder that you have one.** Every app on this list assumes you'll remember to open it. FaithWall is the piece that makes that assumption true, by putting the request where you'll see it dozens of times before you forget it again.

sections.text: Here's what actually kills a **prayer journal app** habit: you write three entries in the first week, feel good about it, and then life gets loud. The app sits on page three of your home screen for a month. When you finally open it again, half the requests are stale — either answered without you noticing, or abandoned so long ago you can't remember why you wrote them. That isn't a discipline failure. It's a retrieval problem. A journal that lives behind an app icon competes with every other app icon for your attention, and it loses. FaithWall skips the icon entirely and puts the request on the one surface you check without opening anything at all.

sections.content: A judgment call, not a feature comparison: if you've abandoned a prayer journal app before, the app probably wasn't the problem. Pair whichever one you pick with something that resurfaces the request without your having to remember it exists — that's the actual gap FaithWall fills.

sections.text: Is there a free prayer journal app for iPhone?

Yes — Prayer Notebook and PrayerMate are both free with no required subscription. Amen. and Echo Prayer are free to start, with an optional paid tier for extras like AI prompts or the ECHO+ group features.
Does FaithWall work as a prayer journal?

No, not as a standalone record — FaithWall doesn't store dated entries or an answered-prayer archive. It's the lock-screen layer that sits alongside a real journal app like Echo Prayer, keeping today's request visible so the journal itself doesn't go unopened for weeks. For the wider setup — alarms, widgets, Focus modes — see the [prayer life on iPhone hub](/prayer-life-iphone), and if you want alarms on top of the lock-screen layer, [our prayer reminders setup](/blog/prayer-reminders-on-iphone) covers that pairing.
